cues: Addresses were once grouped into classes by their first octet.
Class A, for huge networks, up to one two six.
Class B, one two eight to one nine one.
Class C, one nine two to two two three, with two hundred and fifty four hosts each.
D is for multicast and E is reserved.
One two seven is loopback, meaning this computer, and three private ranges are reused inside every school and home, sharing one public address through NAT.
